title: Comparison from a general configuration
statement: Let $Sigma$ be a type with decidable equality, let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be an input word over $Sigma$, choose distinct work-tape indices $fst,snd in k$, choose words $u,v$ over $Sigma$, and let $d$ be a configuration on input $x$ whose state is the running state. Suppose that, for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |u|$, tape $fst$ at position $d$'s head position plus $p$ contains the symbol prescribed by storing $u$ contiguously from position zero; assume the analogous condition for tape $snd$ and word $v$. Then there exists a natural number $delta\le	ext{min}(|u|,|v|)$ such that after $2delta+2$ steps the machine is in configuration $d$ with only its state changed to completed with the truth value of $u=v$; before that time it has not entered either completed state. At every time up to and including $2delta+2$, the heads of tapes $fst$ and $snd$ remain between their respective initial positions minus one and initial positions plus $delta$, inclusive, and every other work-tape head remains at its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: $Sigma$ is a type with decidable equality
tape $fst$ agrees with the buffered word $u$ at every offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |u|$
tape $snd$ agrees with the buffered word $v$ at every offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |v|$
caveat: The source uses the precise buffered-tape convention, including blank cells outside the word; that convention is summarized in the hypothesis.
